This article also reports that, because of the snowmobile industry, approximately 140 resorts in the Arrowhead Region of northeast Minnesota alone were open to snowmobilers last season; and, obviously, all ancillary businesses—grocery stores, restaurants, service stations, and bars — enjoyed additional new business that they would not have had were it not for the sport of snowmobiling.
Although the same volume of business cannot be cited for all the snowbelt states, it is obvious that, in total, the sport of snowmobiling has made a significant economic impact in various areas of the United States, in turn, directly and indirectly affecting other aspects of the American way of life, including family recreational interests, occupation, income, and the environmental impacts resulting from snowmobile use.
An impressive increase in the last few years in the sales and use of other types of recreational vehicles, including motorcycles, dune buggies, ATVs, and other motorized vehicles can also be cited. Again, the volume of such use varies, depending on the particular sections of the United States.
More meaningful, perhaps, is the CEQ requirement that social-economic impacts of Federal actions be cited within human impact phases of environmental statement preparation.
14. Strengthening of family ties through ORV use
In response to the statement on page 12 of the draft ORV environmental statement to the effect that ORV use can strengthen family ties, there were at least 12 incoming responses which challenged this statement. In summary, these comments were as follows:
#19 1. Alaska Conservation Society  felt that this statement is undocumented.
#22 2. Fairbanks Environmental Center  felt that statement is absurd and without evidence.
#26 3. Friends of the Earth  challenged documentation of statement and urged that it be removed from the environmental statement.
#73 4. Idaho Environmental Council  found this statement objectionable.
#54 5. Sierra Club  felt that case for ORV strengthening family relationships should be proven.
#62 6. Natural Resources Defense Council  felt that statement should be treated separately from environmental issue.
#82 7. Florida International University  felt claim that ORV strengthens family ties is spurious.
#16 8. State of Virginia  claimed that just "saying" there is reason to believe that family relationships are strengthened by these activities is hardly a documented statement of favorable impact upon the environment.
